sign: Mind the carts. The winding tower rings at every shift.

lines: Pit Keeper Dorn: The warm spring comes straight up from the deep seams. Rest here.
Trader Wilma: Gear for the deep and brews for the brave.
trader.action: shop tonic strong_tonic max_tonic remedy cooling_gel wake_bell spark_drop revival_leaf dash_brew guard_brew

lines: Smith Holt: You came up the Steps without a pry bar? Brave or daft.
Smith Holt: Take this one. Sluice wheels, stuck carts, rusty grates: lean on it and they give.
Smith Holt: Bring me ore some day and I'll make that bar sing.

shift: Miner Pell-Anne: The lower seams cracked in the storm. Nobody goes below the second level now.

lines: Driver Bram: Valley Coach, Copperfold stop. Mind your head, the roof is low.
Cart Pusher Edda: Back and forth, back and forth. The carts don't push themselves.
Cart Pusher Edda: The rails stopped humming since the Rift was sealed. Good riddance.
Lamp Girl Sorrel: I light the pit lamps when the day shift comes up. Then I count stars.
Lamp Girl Sorrel: The stars look closer now. Mum says that's just clean air.
Foreman Cobb: Dawn at the tower, noon at the tower, dusk at the spring. Some say I live at the tower.
Foreman Cobb: The deep seams stopped shaking. We'll open the lower levels again, slowly.
Old Miner Hask: Forty years below. Now I watch the young ones go down and come up.
Old Miner Hask: The mountain breathes easy again. I can hear it, you know.
Pedlar Maud: Copperfold nails by day, Wrenhollow rope by evening. Everyone needs both.
Pedlar Maud: Business is up since the Rift closed. People buy things when they're not scared.
